behavior: An expert soarer that spends long periods aloft with few wingbeats, steering with its forked tail. It snatches fish and squid from the water’s surface and also pursues other seabirds to steal dropped or regurgitated prey. Breeding is colonial; males display by inflating the red throat sac.
field_marks: Very large, lightly built seabird with extremely long, narrow, angular wings.
Long, deeply forked tail, often held closed so it appears pointed.
Long silvery-gray bill with a strongly hooked tip; dark eye, with a blue-gray eye-ring most evident on adult females.
Adult male glossy black with a conspicuous scarlet inflatable throat sac during display.
Adult female black with a clean white breast; juveniles show a white head and underparts.
Legs and feet are unusually short and small—dark gray-black in males and flesh-pink in females.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical marine waters, from shallow coastal lagoons to the open ocean. Nests and roosts colonially in mangroves, low trees, and shrubs on islands.
